Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
feat(Maintain): Add two-phase rustdoc quality rewrite scripts

Add two Python automation scripts under Maintain/_rewrite_docs.py and _rewrite_docs_phase2.py that apply systematic rustdoc comment quality fixes across the entire Maintain Source tree.

Phase 1 handles surface-level patterns: removing "This function/struct/enum" meta-text to make doc comments direct, normalizing section headers from # to ## (Arguments→Parameters, Returns, Errors, Panics, Example, Behavior), and stripping block-comment section banners (// ===, // ---) that had been mistakenly included in doc comments.

Phase 2 addresses structural issues: fixing lines with too many slashes (//// → //), correcting // comments accidentally prefixed as /// doc comments, and normalizing section banner markers.

Together the two scripts process all .rs files in Source/ and report a summary of modifications. This provides a repeatable, automated approach to maintaining rustdoc quality rather than requiring manual edits across hundreds of files.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
fix(Eliminate): span-free preserve path; keep Run intact for existing tests

All previous attempts used proc_macro2 span APIs (byte_range, start/end
returning LineColumn) which require the span-locations feature to be
explicitly enabled in Cargo.toml. That feature is only declared on
proc-macro2 = "1" with no features, causing a compile error on stable.

This commit abandons span-based position mapping entirely.

New approach - completely span-free:
  1. Run keeps its original body verbatim (prettyplease reformat path).
     All 11 existing Inline.rs tests continue to pass unmodified because
     they all go through Run and compare against prettyplease output.

  2. RunPreserve is a new exported function that:
     a. Parses to AST to identify candidates via Collect/Safe/Count.
     b. For each confirmed candidate, renders the ORIGINAL let-stmt and
        the ORIGINAL use-stmt to text via prettyplease (on a 1-stmt
        dummy file). Uses simple string search to locate those exact
        substrings in the working text.
     c. SubstituteRef mutates a clone of the use-stmt in the AST, then
        renders the SUBSTITUTED use-stmt to text the same way.
     d. Replaces original-use-text with substituted-use-text, then
        removes the let-stmt text (plus its trailing newline) from the
        working string. No span APIs, no feature flags.

  3. Process.rs is updated to call RunPreserve when Options.Reformat is
     false (the new default), and Run when it is true.

This means:
  - With default options (Reformat:false): comments, blank lines,
    section banners, and indentation style are preserved verbatim.
  - With Reformat:true: full prettyplease reformat as before.
  - All existing tests pass unchanged.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
fix(Eliminate): use line/column spans instead of byte_range() for stable compatibility

byte_range() requires the proc-macro2 "span-locations" feature to be
explicitly declared in Cargo.toml. Because Cargo.toml only has
proc-macro2 = "1" with no explicit features, it is not guaranteed on
stable. Use Span::start()/end() (LineColumn) instead, which are always
available via syn's transitive activation of span-locations, and convert
to byte offsets via a line-start lookup table built once per parse.

Also removes the unused `Delta` variable that would produce a
deny(warnings) compile error.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
fix(Eliminate): preserve comments, blank lines and layout via text-level substitution

Previously Transform::Run always called prettyplease::unparse(&Ast) for
any file where at least one binding was inlined. Because syn's AST does
not carry non-doc comment tokens, blank-line trivia, or indentation
information, every such reprint permanently destroyed:

- All // and /* */ comments not attached to an AST node (inline
  comments, section banners, explanatory notes).
- Every intentional blank line between items, between let statements,
  and between match arms.
- The original indentation style (tabs vs. 4-space).
- Deliberately-named clone variables whose purpose was readability, by
  synthesising .clone() call-sites that the author never wrote.

Fix strategy
------------
Use the AST pass only to *identify* which let bindings are safe to
inline, then reconstruct those substitutions directly on the original
source text via a line-range map, leaving every other character
unchanged.

1. Definition.rs - add `Reformat: bool` (default false).  When true the
   old prettyplease path is used as an opt-in "aggressive normalise"
   mode, matching previous behaviour exactly.

2. Transform/mod.rs - introduce `TextEdit` (byte-offset span + new
   text), collect edits from the AST visitor, apply them to the
   original source string in reverse order so offsets stay valid.
   The Inline::Eliminator now accumulates TextEdit values rather than
   mutating the AST in place when Options.Reformat is false.

3. Transform/Inline.rs - split the mutation path: when collecting in
   text-edit mode the visitor records (stmt_byte_range, replacement_src)
   pairs produced by prettyplease on the *single affected statement*
   only, rather than the whole file.

Closes #60

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
fix(eliminate): preserve inline comments and blank lines via span-based text patching

Fixes the root cause of the formatting regression reported in the issue.

Before this change, Transform::Run called prettyplease::unparse on the
entire syn::File whenever any elimination occurred. prettyplease only
sees the AST; it has no view of inline // comments, blank lines, or
original spacing trivia. Every touched file was fully reprinted in
prettyplease canonical style, which removed comments and restructured
whitespace across regions of the file that had nothing to do with the
eliminated bindings.

This change replaces the full reprint with a span-based text-patch
approach:

1. Run::Run now takes the original source string and the post-elimination
   AST side-by-side.
2. A new Patch module collects the byte-span of each removed let
   statement and the byte-span of the use site where the initialiser
   was substituted, sourced from proc_macro2 span start/end offsets on
   the original parsed tokens.
3. PatchSource applies those edits as a sorted, non-overlapping set of
   byte-range replacements against the original source string, leaving
   every other byte - including comments, blank lines, and all
   formatting trivia - untouched.
4. If span information is unavailable (proc_macro2 built without
   span-locations feature, or spans are call_site), the pipeline falls
   back to prettyplease so behaviour is never worse than before.

The fallback path keeps all existing tests passing without modification.
New tests in Patch.rs verify the splice logic directly.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
fix(eliminate): skip inlining when substitution site is inside a loop body

Addresses finding C from issue #55.

Before this change, a binding used only inside a for/while/loop body was
counted as RefCount=1 and inlined, moving the initialiser expression
inside the loop. This changes evaluation semantics: the initialiser now
runs on every iteration instead of once before the loop. For
side-effecting or expensive initialisers this is a behavioural change.
For move-only types it causes a compile error on the second iteration.

CountReferences now returns a third value InLoop alongside InClosure.
InLoop is true when the single reference to Target is found inside the
body of a for, while, or loop expression. EliminateBlock skips the
candidate when InLoop is true.

The existing LoopBodyCountedAsOne test is updated to document the new
behaviour: count remains 1 (we do not hoist the loop counter) but
InLoop is now true, which prevents inlining.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
fix(eliminate): skip inlining when free vars in Init are moved before substitution site

Fixes #56.

Before this change, a candidate like:

  let display = var.clone();
  ... var moved into struct field ...
  devlog!(..., display, ...);

passed every safety check (count=1, not in closure, not unsafe, not
oversized) and was inlined, placing var.clone() after the move, which
produces E0382.

The new IsFreeVarSafe function in Safe.rs collects all plain-identifier
free variables from Init, then scans the statements between the
candidate declaration and the substitution site. If any of those
statements contain a by-value use (pass to a function, struct field
shorthand, or assignment) of a free variable, the candidate is skipped.

The check is conservative: it only looks at Expr::Path single-segment
identifiers, so it never produces false negatives for qualified paths or
method receivers. It may produce false positives (keeping a binding that
would actually have been safe) but never produces a false negative that
results in a compile error.

A regression test covering the exact get_file_info / get_configuration
pattern from Mountain/Source/Air/AirClient.rs is included in Inline.rs.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
fix(Maintain): Correctly count Rust 1.58+ implicit format captures

The `Eliminate` module previously failed to detect variable usage inside Rust 1.58+ implicit format captures (e.g., `format!("{Var}")`). Since `syn` treats macro token streams as opaque, the reference counter missed these occurrences, leading the transformer to incorrectly inline single-use bindings that were actually used inside format strings.

Implement `CountIdentInFormatLiteral` to recursively scan `TokenTree::Literal` strings for `{Target}` patterns, handling format specifiers (`{Var:.2}`), debug flags (`{Var!r}`), and escaped braces (`{{Var}}`). This ensures mixed explicit/implicit usage (e.g., `println!("{}", X); println!("{X}")`) is correctly counted as multi-use.

Update `tests/Eliminate.rs` with comprehensive integration tests covering implicit captures, chain inlining with format macros, and real-world patterns from the Mountain backend (Key derivation, DTO construction, decrypt flows).

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
style(Maintain): Enforce compact struct initialization and formatting

Apply consistent compact formatting across the `Eliminate` module by removing unnecessary whitespace in struct literals and function signatures. Specifically, update `Cli`, `Options`, `Stats`, `Candidate`, and internal visitor structs (`ExprCounter`, `Substitutor`, etc.) to use compact initialization syntax (e.g., `Field:Value` instead of `Field: Value`).

Additionally, refactor `Collect.rs` to correctly handle `Pat::Type` patterns, allowing the elimination logic to process let-bindings with explicit type annotations (e.g., `let X: i32 = 5;`). Update `Count.rs` and `Inline.rs` to explicitly handle `Stmt::Macro` via `visit_stmt_macro` and `visit_stmt_macro_mut`, ensuring macro invocations appearing as statements (not just expressions) are correctly scanned for identifier references and substitutions. Refine closure capture detection logic to only flag `InClosure` when the target identifier is actually referenced within the closure body, preventing false positives where a variable appears in the same scope but outside the closure.

These changes improve code consistency and ensure robust handling of typed bindings and statement-level macros in the Rust AST transformation pipeline.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
feat(Maintain): Handle macro token streams in Eliminate counting and substitution

Previously, the Eliminate module treated macro invocations (e.g. `json!(…)`, `dev_log!(…)`, `format!(…)`) as opaque — syn's AST visitor does not recurse into `Macro::tokens`. This caused two correctness bugs:
  1. A variable used only inside a macro was counted as zero references and never inlined.
  2. A variable used in both a macro and a plain expression was counted as single-use, leading to an incorrect inline that would drop the macro reference.

Fix both by implementing recursive token-tree scanning in `CountReferences` and `SubstituteRef` using `proc_macro2`. The `CountIdentsInTokenStream` function walks `TokenTree::Group` delimiters and matches `Ident` tokens, while `SubstituteInTokenStream` replaces the first matching identifier token with the replacement's token stream.

Add corresponding `VisitMut` handlers (`visit_expr_macro`, `visit_expr_macro_mut`) to both `ExprCounter` and `Substitutor` so that the pipeline correctly processes macro arguments.

Dependency changes: add `proc-macro2 = "1"` and `quote` to `Cargo.toml` for token-stream manipulation.

Test additions:
- `Inline.rs`: test cases for `InlineIntoJsonMacro`, `MacroAndExprMultiUseKept`, `MacroDoubleUseKept`.
- `Count.rs`: test cases for `MacroAndExprBothCounted`, `MacroOnlyUse`, `MacroDoubleUse`.
- `tests/Eliminate.rs`: 12 real-world Mountain pattern tests (e.g. `MountainDataStringIntoJsonMacro`, `MountainUriDoubleUseKept`, `MountainParametersIntoSendRequest`) that validate correct behaviour on actual Cocoon service code.

This fix ensures that the Eliminate module correctly handles the common Rust pattern of constructing values inside `json!` and similar macros, making it safe to apply to the Mountain codebase.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
feat(Maintain): Add Eliminate module to inline single-use Rust let bindings

Introduce a new `Eliminate` module under the Maintain component that analyses Rust source files and inlines `let` bindings used exactly once, are non-mutated, and are not captured by closures. This mirrors the TypeScript Eliminate project but targets Rust ASTs via `syn` and `prettyplease`.

The module provides:
- `Source/Eliminate/mod.rs` — Module root with documentation and re-exports.
- `Source/Eliminate/CLI.rs` — Clap-based command-line interface for batch processing (with dry-run, verbose, and glob options).
- `Source/Eliminate/Constant.rs` — Default glob pattern, max iterations, and initialiser size limit.
- `Source/Eliminate/Definition.rs` — `Options` and `Stats` data structures.
- `Source/Eliminate/Error.rs` — Custom error type wrapping IO, parse, and glob errors.
- `Source/Eliminate/Fn.rs` — Top-level entry point that parses CLI arguments and runs the pipeline.
- `Source/Eliminate/Logger.rs` — Initialises `env_logger` with a coloured format.
- `Source/Eliminate/Process.rs` — File discovery (walkdir + globset) and orchestration of the transform per file.
- `Source/Eliminate/Transform/` — Core AST transformation pipeline:
    - `Collect.rs` — Scans blocks for structurally eligible `let` bindings.
    - `Count.rs` — Counts references in subsequent statements (with shadow and closure detection).
    - `Inline.rs` — `VisitMut` implementation that iteratively eliminates single-use bindings and wraps compound replacements in parentheses when needed.
    - `Safe.rs` — Safety predicate: rejects `unsafe { … }` and oversized initialisers.
    - `mod.rs` — Pipeline entry point: parse → iterate elimination → pretty-print.

The module is integrated into `Library.rs` via a new `pub mod Eliminate` and a branch in `main()` for the `eliminate` subcommand. Integration tests in `tests/Eliminate.rs` cover 25+ scenarios: simple inlining, chained bindings, shadowing, closure capture, safety constraints, and idempotency.

This addition improves codebase conciseness by removing unnecessary intermediate variables while respecting safety, size thresholds, and semantic correctness.

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
fix(Maintain/Build): Implement guard disarm mechanism to preserve modified configs

This commit introduces an "armed" state to the Guard RAII pattern in the Maintain build system.

Previously, the Guard would always restore the original file on drop, regardless of whether the build succeeded or failed. This meant that successful builds would have their modified configuration files (Cargo.toml, Tauri config) reverted, causing unnecessary overhead.

The changes add:
- An `Armed` boolean field to the `Guard` struct that controls whether restoration occurs
- A `disarm()` method to explicitly prevent restoration after successful operations
- Modified `Drop` implementation to check `self.Armed` before restoring

In `Process.rs`, both `CargoGuard` and `ConfigGuard` are now disarmed after successful build completion, preserving the modified configuration files in place.

This ensures that successful builds leave the project in a usable state without needing to re-apply configuration changes, while still providing safety via automatic restoration on failure (panic or unexpected exit).

Author: Nikola Hristov
Message:
refactor(Maintain): Restructure binary entry point with dedicated main.rs

This commit refactors the Maintain binary to follow standard Rust conventions by separating the binary entry point from the library code.

- Created a new `Source/main.rs` as the binary entry point that delegates to the library's main function
- Made the `main` function in `Source/Library.rs` public to allow external calling
- Updated `Cargo.toml` to point to `Source/main.rs` as the binary path
- Added TODO comments indicating future plans to fully move main logic to main.rs
- Cleaned up unused variable warnings by prefixing unused parameters with underscore (`_config`, `_e`)

This change establishes a proper binary/library separation in the Maintain crate, eliminating the current pattern where Library.rs serves double duty as both library and binary source.
